title: Equivariant Borel Moore Correspondence Convolution And Constructible Ext

items.title: Complex-oriented diagonal Thom classes realize exceptional exchange on supports
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the analytic six-functor and equivariant constructible suppliers below. In the analytic constructible six-functor setting, let $M$ be a smooth complex manifold of pure dimension $d$, and let $A\to M$, $B\to M$ be algebraic maps whose fiber product is $T$. Assume the supplied duality construction has localization, tensor-Hom adjunction, coherent exchange maps, and the smooth orientation normalized by the positive compactly supported generator on a complex coordinate ball ([[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]]), with its equivariant constructible form supplied by [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]. The refined pullback of dualizing classes on the support $A\times B$ by the ambient middle diagonal $M\to M\times M$ is the operation induced by the mate $a^*q^!\to b^!u^*$ of $b_!a^*\to u^*q_!$, after tensor evaluation and dualizing transitivity. It equals cap product with the positive middle-diagonal Thom class and lowers Borel-Moore degree by $2d$, even for singular, nontransverse supports. Ordered iterated diagonals are compatible with composed refined operations. For a complex vector bundle, zero-section self-intersection is cap product with its oriented Euler class.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Sources: Ginzburg, Geometric methods in representation theory, SS2 (convolution in Borel-Moore homology: the general supported construction, its dependence on the ambient orientations, and associativity; PDF pp. 7-10) and SS5 Proposition 5.1 (the diagonal-restriction chain identifying the convolution algebra with Ext; PDF pp. 18-19); Varshavsky, Lefschetz-Verdier trace formula, SS0.3-0.4 and SS1.1 (adjunction, base-change mates, projection formula and correspondence composition; PDF pp. 5-8). Step 1 (diagonal normal model): for the diagonal $i:M\hookrightarrow M\times M$ a tubular normal chart has normal pair $(\mathbb C^d,\mathbb C^d\setminus\{0\})$, whose relative cohomology is $k$ in degree $2d$ and zero in other degrees by the long exact sequence of the sphere and the contraction of the disk; hence $i^!k_{M\times M}=k_M[-2d]$ under the positive local generator. The orientation sheaf has trivial transition signs because a complex transition has positive real determinant, so compatible local positive generators specify its global isomorphism with no higher-degree gluing ambiguity, and this is exactly the Thom class of the complex normal bundle $TM$. Step 2 (supported tensor-Hom evaluation): for a closed embedding $z:Z\hookrightarrow N$ the injective model $z^!=z^{-1}\Gamma_Z$ and its localization triangle identify $R\operatorname{Hom}(z_*k_Z,F)$ with $R\Gamma_Z(F)$, so on a closed support in an ambient manifold exceptional restriction is computed by relative sections and tensor evaluation realizes cup/cap product of supported classes as the tensor-Hom evaluation map. Pulling the orientation map of Step 1 back to $A\times B$ along the support square and applying tensor-Hom adjunction gives the mate exchange: its left adjoint is the base-change map $b_!a^*\to u^*q_!$ followed by evaluation, and conversely the right adjoint of this base-change evaluation is the pulled-back supported orientation map. This is an equality of the two explicit adjoint maps, not an inference from equality of their values after forgetting support, so cap product with the Thom class and the exceptional exchange agree without a transversality assertion on the support. Step 3 (iterated diagonals and Euler class): for two ordered diagonals the normal model is the ordered direct sum of their complex normal bundles; on the product of normal coordinate disks the relative cup product of the two positive generators evaluates to $+1$ on the ordered product disk, which is the positive generator of the sum, and local uniqueness as in Step 1 with base-change mate pasting as in Step 2 gives the composed operation on every support. For a vector-bundle zero section its pullback of the Thom class is by definition the Euler class, so applying zero-section refined pullback after zero-section pushforward caps with this class. All real degrees $2d$ are even, so ordering the normal summands introduces no additional sign. Only the declared localization, tensor-Hom, exchange, orientation and trace clauses are used; the remaining steps are choice-free.

items.title: Equivariant Borel–Moore homology and oriented correspondence convolution
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the equivariant
constructible and Borel-stabilization suppliers. Let $G=\prod_v\mathrm{GL}_{n_v}(\mathbb C)$,
let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, and use bounded algebraically constructible complexes of
$k$-sheaves in the analytic topology, in the equivariant derived category
$D^b_{G,c}(-;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]].
All functors are derived.

**Dualizing normalization and Borel–Moore homology.** The equivariant dualizing object is
normalized by $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$, rather than by the dimension of the quotient stack; here
$\omega_X=a_X^!k$ is the ordinary constructible dualizing object and
$\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$ for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$
([[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]). Define
$$H_j^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;k)=H_G^{-j}(X,\omega_X^G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{G,c}(X;k)}(k_X,\omega_X^G[-j]).$$
Equivalently, for a free smooth approximation: a $G$-invariant open subset $U$ of a
finite-dimensional complex $G$-representation on which $G$ acts freely, and
$b=\dim_{\mathbb C}U-\dim_{\mathbb C}G$, the group is the eventual stable value
$H_{j+2b}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X\times_GU;k)$; existence of the stable value and its independence of the
approximation are supplied by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]. Ordinary
Borel–Moore homology is the case $G=1$ in the same formula, i.e.
$H_j^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;k)=\operatorname{Hom}(k_X,\omega_X[-j])$, and the smooth complex orientation
gives $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$ for $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d$.

**Correspondences.** Let $f_i:X_i\to E$ be finitely many proper $G$-equivariant algebraic maps
with $X_i$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d_i$. Put $Z_{ij}=X_i\times_EX_j$ (reduced
analytically), $T_{ijk}=X_i\times_EX_j\times_EX_k$, and let $h:T_{ijk}\to Z_{ik}$ forget the
middle point; it is proper, being the base change of $f_j$. The first coordinate is the source.
For $a\in H_p^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij})$, $b\in H_q^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{jk})$, define
$$a*b=h_*\Delta_{X_j}^{!}(a\boxtimes b)\in H_{p+q-2d_j}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ik}).$$
Here $\Delta_{X_j}^{!}$ is the refined oriented middle-diagonal operation on supports of
[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]]: it
restricts the external class to $T_{ijk}$ by the Thom class of the complex normal bundle $TX_j$
of $X_j\hookrightarrow X_j\times X_j$. It is defined on arbitrary closed supports; no
transversality of $Z_{ij}$ and $Z_{jk}$ is assumed. Proper pushforward is the dualizing trace.
The ordered coordinates are $(i,j,j,k)$, and the two middle factors are contracted without a
permutation. If intermediate indices differ, the product is set to zero. Put degree $d_i+d_j-p$
on the $(i,j)$ corner. The normalized diagonal class $[\Delta_{X_i}]$ has corner degree zero.

**Sheaf model.** The sheaf model of the refined Thom operation uses the exchange morphism
$u^*v^!\to v'^!u'^*$ for the middle Cartesian square: with $u:Z_{ij}\to X_j$,
$v:Z_{jk}\to X_j$, $T=Z_{ij}\times_{X_j}Z_{jk}$ and projections $v':T\to Z_{ij}$,
$u':T\to Z_{jk}$, the morphism is obtained as the adjunction mate of proper base change
$u'_!v'^*\cong v^*u_!$. It is a morphism, not an asserted isomorphism for arbitrary supports.
Its orientation is fixed by the Thom class restricting to $+1$ on every positively
complex-oriented normal fiber. Agreement of this model with the stated refined geometric
operation, and compatibility with composition, are proved in
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]] after the
foundational six-functor inputs are available.

**Well-formedness.** The definition is independent of the chosen free smooth approximation
because the stable Borel value exists and stabilizes by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]; the product is
defined because the refined middle-diagonal operation of
[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]] is
defined on arbitrary closed supports and $h$ is proper, so its dualizing trace is available; the
degree bookkeeping is fixed by the pure complex dimension $d_j$ of the middle factor. The claim
that the sheaf model and the geometric operation agree, and that the product is compatible with
composition and units, is not assumed here: it is the content of
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]], which is
recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that theorem depends on this
definition. The Axiom of Choice is consumed exactly through the three cited suppliers, whose
constructions (equivariant descent, injective replacements, Borel stabilization) declare it;
the definition itself introduces no further choice principle.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Sources: Ginzburg, Geometric methods in representation theory, SS2 (the supported convolution product, its dependence on the ambient orientations, and associativity; PDF pp. 7-10) and SS5 Proposition 5.1 (the corner normalization; PDF pp. 18-19); Varagnolo-Vasserot, SS1.1-1.10 (equivariant Borel-Moore corners and the source-first convention; PDF pp. 1-12). Step 1 (ambient object and normalization): the equivariant category and its degreewise-finite Morphism spaces are those of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]], and the stable Borel value is supplied by [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]; the dualizing normalization $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$ is the normalized one fixed by [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]], not the unnormalized quotient-stack shift. Step 2 (the geometric product): $h$ is proper because it is the base change of the proper map $f_j$, so the proper pushforward in the product is the dualizing trace; the refined diagonal restriction $\Delta_{X_j}^{!}$ on arbitrary closed supports is the operation of [[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]], which also proves that it agrees with the mate of proper base change used by the sheaf model. No transversality or smoothness of the $Z_{ij}$ is used. Step 3 (degrees and unit): the middle factor $X_j$ has pure complex dimension $d_j$, so the refined diagonal operation lowers Borel-Moore degree by $2d_j$ and the product lands in $H_{p+q-2d_j}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ik})$; the corner degree $d_i+d_j-p$ makes the diagonal class $[\Delta_{X_i}]$ have degree $d_i+d_i-2d_i=0$, and nonmatching indices multiply to zero by the definition. The definition is otherwise choice-free.

items.title: Proper-pushforward Ext is equivariant Borel–Moore homology of the fiber product
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the constructible six-functor and Borel-stabilization suppliers. Use the constructible equivariant setting $D^b_{G,c}(E;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] and proper $G$-equivariant algebraic maps $f_i:X_i\to E$ with smooth sources $X_i$ of pure complex dimension $d_i$, as in [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]. Put $L_i=f_{i!}k_{X_i}[d_i]$. For every integer $r$ and every pair $(i,j)$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$\Phi_{ij}^r:\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{G,c}(E;k)}(L_i,L_j[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{d_i+d_j-r}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij};k).$$
All groups are degreewise finite-dimensional for these finite-type algebraic varieties and $G$; no finite-dimensionality of their direct sum over all degrees is asserted. The isomorphism is equivariant-cohomology linear, commutes with enlargement of the Borel approximation, and is natural in constructible coefficient morphisms before smooth orientation is applied. No semismallness, decomposition theorem, purity, or smoothness of $E$ or $Z_{ij}$ is required.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Source: Ginzburg, Geometric methods in representation theory, SS5 Proposition 5.1 (the Cartesian-square chain $H^\bullet(Z,D_Z)\cong H^\bullet(N_\Delta,i^!(L^\vee\boxtimes L))\cong\operatorname{Ext}^\bullet(L,L)$; PDF pp. 18-19) together with Varshavsky, Lefschetz-Verdier trace formula, SS0.3-0.4 and SS1.1 (adjunction, base-change mates, projection formula, dualizing transitivity; PDF pp. 5-8). Step 1 (adjunction chain): write $p:Z_{ij}\to X_i$, $q:Z_{ij}\to X_j$ and $t=r+d_j-d_i$. Removing the source shift by $[-d_i]$ and using $f_{i!}\dashv f_i^!$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}_E(f_{i!}k_i,f_{j!}k_j[t])=\operatorname{Hom}_{X_i}(k_i,f_i^!f_{j!}k_j[t])$. In the Cartesian square with lower arrow $f_j$ and right arrow $f_i$, the dual mate of proper base change of [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]] gives $f_i^!f_{j!}k_j=p_*q^!k_j$ because both maps are proper, so $p^*\dashv p_*$ identifies the group with $\operatorname{Hom}_{Z_{ij}}(k_Z,q^!k_j[t])$. This is the complete cornerwise chain, including negative $r$. Step 2 (orientation and degree): smooth orientation on $X_j$ says $k_j=\omega_{X_j}[-2d_j]$, and transitivity of the exceptional inverse image gives $q^!k_j=\omega_Z[-2d_j]$; hence the group is $\operatorname{Hom}(k_Z,\omega_Z[r-d_i-d_j])$, which is exactly $H_{d_i+d_j-r}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij};k)$ in the normalization fixed by [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]. At a finite Borel approximation of dimension offset $b$, $X_j\times_GU$ has dimension $d_j+b$ while the descended complex retains the shift $d_j$, so the identical calculation gives ordinary Borel-Moore degree $d_i+d_j+2b-r$; removing $2b$ gives the stated equivariant degree, and no stack-dimension shift is inserted into $\omega_X^G$. Step 3 (naturality, linearity, finiteness): every map in the chain is an adjunction, base-change, or orientation map supplied naturally; they commute with approximation transition pullbacks by [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]], so they induce an isomorphism in each stable degree. Coherent scalar pullback from the base point and the projection formula give equivariant-cohomology linearity, and degreewise finiteness is exactly that lemma's conclusion, not a boundedness assertion about the total equivariant Ext. Smoothness is used only for the orientation on $X_j$ and properness only in base change and in the identification of the two pushforwards.

items.title: Verdier-duality identification intertwines Yoneda product and oriented convolution
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the constructible six-functor and Borel-stabilization suppliers. For the data and cornerwise maps $\Phi$ of [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]], let $\alpha:L_i\to L_j[r]$, $\beta:L_j\to L_k[s]$. With multiplication $\alpha*\beta=\beta[r]\circ\alpha$ one has
$$\Phi_{ik}^{r+s}(\beta[r]\circ\alpha)=\Phi_{ij}^r(\alpha)*\Phi_{jk}^s(\beta).$$
Here the right product is the external-product, refined middle-diagonal Thom intersection, proper-pushforward convolution of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], not a product transported by definition from Ext. The map sends $\operatorname{id}_{L_i}$ to $[\Delta_{X_i}]$. Consequently the direct sum of all corners is an isomorphism of unital graded algebras with this opposite-composition convention; nonmatching corners multiply to zero.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Sources: Ginzburg, Geometric methods in representation theory, SS2 (associativity of the supported convolution and its dependence on the ambient orientation; PDF pp. 8-10) and SS5 Proposition 5.1 (the algebra identification, whose compatibility of products is stated there to be proved in [Chriss-Ginzburg, Theorem 8.6.7]; PDF pp. 18-19), together with Varshavsky SS1.1.6(b) (proper-pushforward composition by base-change pasting; PDF pp. 6-8). The product-compatibility clause is reconstructed locally below rather than cited. Step 1 (typed correspondences): at an ordinary finite Borel approximation, write $A=Z_{ij}$, $B=Z_{jk}$, $C=Z_{ik}$, $T=T_{ijk}$ and the projections $p,q,u,v,a,b,h,\ell,m$ of the typed triple diagram, with $qa=ub$, $pa=\ell h$, $vb=mh$; the middle square is Cartesian and every displayed projection is proper. Put $t=r+d_j-d_i$ and $w=s+d_k-d_j$; the adjoint representatives of $\Phi(\alpha)$ and $\Phi(\beta)$ are cohomological correspondences $U:q_!k_A\to k_j[t]$ and $V:v_!k_B\to k_k[w]$, with kernel forms $\kappa:k_A\to q^!k_j[t]$ and $\lambda:k_B\to v^!k_k[w]$. Step 2 (the explicit composite): let $\mathrm{BC}:b_!a^*\xrightarrow{\sim}u^*q_!$ be proper base change and form $W:(vb)_!k_T=v_!b_!a^*k_A\xrightarrow{v_!\mathrm{BC}}v_!u^*q_!k_A\xrightarrow{v_!u^*U}v_!k_B[t]\xrightarrow{V[t]}k_k[t+w]$. Its adjoint $k_T\to(vb)^!k_k[t+w]$ is exactly the composite $k_T\xrightarrow{a^*\kappa}a^*q^!k_j[t]\to b^!u^*k_j[t]=b^!k_B[t]\xrightarrow{b^!\lambda[t]}(vb)^!k_k[t+w]$, where the middle arrow is the mate exchange of $\mathrm{BC}$; this follows by applying $(vb)_!\dashv(vb)^!$ to both maps, so the defining evaluation of the mate gives precisely the three arrows of $W$ and no exchange isomorphism is assumed. Step 3 (geometric interpretation): place $A\times B$ as its closed support in $X_i\times X_j\times X_j\times X_k$ and pull it back by $\operatorname{id}_{X_i}\times\Delta_{X_j}\times\operatorname{id}_{X_k}$. External product of $\kappa,\lambda$ corresponds by smooth orientation to the external dualizing class; the pulled-back diagonal is defined on this support by the exceptional-pullback exchange of [[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]], contracting the two middle orientation factors, and its dualizing representative is the map of Step 2. Restricting the ambient diagonal to a normal coordinate ball in $X_j$ shows that the exceptional-pullback orientation and the complex Thom class of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]] both take value $+1$ on the ordered real coordinates, so they are the same map and the refined operation is given by the Thom contraction even when the support is singular or nontransverse. Step 4 (push to the third corner): pushing the correspondence on $T$ to $C$ gives $U_C:m_!k_C\xrightarrow{m_!\eta_h}m_!h_*k_T=(vb)_!k_T\xrightarrow{W}k_k[t+w]$, whose kernel form is $k_C\to h_*k_T\to h_*h^!m^!k_k[t+w]\xrightarrow{\epsilon_h}m^!k_k[t+w]$ with $\epsilon_h$ the dualizing proper trace; transitivity identifies the middle dualizing object with $\omega_T[-2d_k+t+w]$ and Step 3 identifies this class with $h_*\Delta_{X_j}^!(\Phi(\alpha)\boxtimes\Phi(\beta))$. Step 5 (composition square on its arrows): the inverse of the chain of [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] sends $U$ to $f_{i!}k_i\xrightarrow{f_{i!}\eta_p}f_{i!}p_*k_A=f_{j!}q_!k_A\xrightarrow{f_{j!}U}f_{j!}k_j[t]$ and $V$ analogously; naturality of $\eta_u$ moves $f_{j!}U$ past the second unit, proper base change identifies the resulting units with the composed unit of $pa=\ell h$, and taking left adjoints gives the identity on $a^*p^*k_i=k_T$ by the two adjunction triangle equations, so both routes give $f_{i!}k_i\xrightarrow{f_{i!}\eta_{pa}}f_{k!}(vb)_!k_T\xrightarrow{f_{k!}W}f_{k!}k_k[t+w]$. The inverse map applied to $U_C$ gives the same expression because the composed-unit formula $\eta_{\ell h}=\ell_*\eta_h\ell^*\circ\eta_\ell$ follows from the same triangle equations, so the whole product square commutes for arbitrary cohomological correspondences before orientation or grading is applied. Step 6 (shifts and units): restoring object shifts gives $t+w=r+s+d_k-d_i$, the corner degrees $d_i+d_j-r$ and $d_j+d_k-s$ add and lose $2d_j$ to give $d_i+d_k-r-s$, and at a finite approximation every incoming degree acquires $2b$; homogeneous maps compose as $V[t]\circ U=\beta[r]\circ\alpha$ with no interchanged factors and no $(-1)^{rs}$ sign, since the normal orientation has even real degree. For $i=j$ the identity inverse-correspondence is the diagonal unit under the adjunction triangle equations, and its kernel is the positive complex diagonal fundamental class by the orientation check of Step 3, so $\Phi(\operatorname{id}_{L_i})=[\Delta X_i]$; product compatibility transfers associativity and these units from composition, and distinct corners are zero on both sides by source/target matching. All foundational six-operation, duality and stabilization clauses are used through the declared suppliers; the remaining arguments are formal.

items.strategy:
Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Sources: Ginzburg, Geometric methods in representation theory, SS2 (convolution with supports) and SS5 Proposition 5.1 (the flag-incidence/Ext dictionary; PDF pp. 7-10, 18-19); Varagnolo-Vasserot SS1.1-1.10 (the quiver-flag incidence spaces, their dimension shifts and the convolution corners; PDF pp. 1-12). Step 1 (incidence as an associated bundle): fix a graded reference flag, whose stabilizer is the product of upper triangular subgroups in the individual $\mathrm{GL}(V_v)$; its orbit $B_
u$ is the product of complete flag varieties $\prod_v\mathrm{Flag}(V_v)$ by [[lem-flag-variety-of-a-vector-space]]. In an ordinary flag chart choose ordered basis vectors compatible with the flags; the stability condition for an arrow $h:v	o w$ says that its matrix coefficient from source position $a$ to target position $b$ vanishes whenever $b>a$ in the full word $
u$. Thus the fiber is a fixed linear subspace $S_
u\subset E_V$, of dimension the sum over arrows of the number of allowed pairs; the stabilizer preserves $S_
u$, and $X_

u}S_

Step 2 (smoothness, projectivity, properness): flag charts are affine spaces and each nontrivial flag factor is smooth projective, so $X_
u$ is smooth of pure dimension $d_
u=\sum_v\dim\mathrm{Flag}(V_v)+\dim S_
u$; stability is the vanishing of the bundle maps $F^a_v	o V_w/F^a_w$ induced by $x_h$, so $X_
u$ is closed in $E_V	imes B_
u$ and $\pi_
u$ is a restriction of the projective product projection; the middle-forgetting map is its base change for $\pi_\eta$, hence proper, although neither its fibers nor the total spaces are asserted smooth. Step 3 (orientations and equivariance): every $X_
u$ has its complex orientation and its diagonal has complex normal bundle $TX_
u$; applying the Thom class of [[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]] to the pulled-back closed support gives the refined diagonal operation of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], whether or not the support is transverse, and proper trace along the map of Step 2 supplies convolution. All constructions use equivariant bundle maps and the invariant complex orientation, so they descend to smooth free approximations; the equivariant setting is that of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] and it is supplied to the Ext and product theorems [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] and [[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]] with exactly the dimension shift $d_
u$, not the dimension of the flag base alone; the Borel approximations have finite CW type by [[thm-constructible-sheaves-admit-finite-stratified-triangulations-and-finite-local-cohomology]]. Step 4 (zero sections and Euler classes): for a rank-$c$ complex bundle the normal pair of its zero section is its oriented disk/sphere pair; multiplication by the positive Thom class defines the Gysin operation, and pulling that class back by the zero section gives its Euler class, which equals the top Chern class by [[thm-top-chern-class-equals-euler-class-of-the-underlying-real-bundle]] on each CW-type approximation component. Smooth complex bundle and flag-bundle maps use the relative orientation, so they have the stated oriented pullbacks, and these operations commute with proper pushforward and Cartesian pullback by the projection formula and trace/base-change mates. This supplies the calculus, not the numerical signed crossing formulas of a geometric KLR presentation.

title: Equivariant Borel Moore Correspondence Convolution And Constructible Ext Examples

items.title: Unequal-dimensional proper pushforwards carry the summed-dimension Ext/Borel–Moore degree
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited constructible and cellular suppliers. For trivial $G$, $E=\mathrm{pt}$, $X_1=\mathrm{pt}$ and $X_2=\mathbb P^1$ with $d_1=0$, $d_2=1$, put $L_1=k$ and $L_2=R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]$ in the setting of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]. Then $\operatorname{Ext}^r(L_1,L_2)$ is $k$ for $r=-1,1$ and zero otherwise, and the corresponding summed-dimension Borel-Moore degrees $d_1+d_2-r$ are $2$ and $0$; the reverse corner $\operatorname{Ext}^r(L_2,L_1)$ has the same two nonzero degrees. The unaugmented shifts $2\dim_{\mathbb C}X_1-r= -r$ and $2\dim_{\mathbb C}X_2-r=2-r$ give the wrong degrees in at least one corner, so the summed $d_1+d_2$ normalization of [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] is the one compatible with the two unequal source dimensions.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Route: for the trivial group take the identity Borel model, so [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] reduces to the ordinary bounded constructible category and $Z_{12}=Z_{21}=\mathbb P^1$. Step 1 (the two objects): $f_1:\mathrm{pt}\to\mathrm{pt}$ is proper and $d_1=0$, so $L_1=k$; $f_2:\mathbb P^1\to\mathrm{pt}$ is proper and $d_2=1$, so $L_2=f_{2!}k_{\mathbb P^1}[1]=R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]$. Step 2 (cohomology of the projective line): $\mathbb P^1=\operatorname{Gr}_1(\mathbb C^2)$ has the finite Schubert CW structure of [[def-stiefel-space-grassmannian-and-tautological-bundle]], [[def-schubert-cells-in-real-and-complex-grassmannians]] and [[thm-schubert-cells-give-the-stable-grassmannian-cw-structure]] with one cell in real dimension $0$ and one in real dimension $2$, and no two cells in adjacent dimensions; the cellular boundary differentials vanish by [[cor-a-cw-complex-with-no-cells-in-adjacent-dimensions-has-zero-cellular-boundary]], so the cellular cochain complex with constant coefficients $k$ computes $H^0(\mathbb P^1,k)=k$, $H^1=0$, $H^2=k$ by [[thm-cellular-cochains-compute-cohomology-with-local-coefficients]], and $R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)\simeq k\oplus k[-2]$. Step 3 (forward corner): $\operatorname{Ext}^r(L_1,L_2)=\operatorname{Hom}(k,R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1+r])=H^{1+r}(\mathbb P^1,k)$ is nonzero exactly for $r=-1$ (from $H^0$) and $r=1$ (from $H^2$), and zero otherwise. Step 4 (reverse corner and degree shift): $\operatorname{Hom}(R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1],k[r])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R\Gamma,k[r-1])$ is nonzero exactly for $r\in\{-1,1\}$ by the same two cohomology groups, so both corners have the same two Ext degrees. By [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] these corners are $H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{1-r}(\mathbb P^1;k)$, which in the normalization of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]] is $H^{2-(1-r)}(\mathbb P^1,k)$: it is $k$ for $1-r=2$ and for $1-r=0$, that is, for the Borel-Moore degrees $2$ and $0$, and vanishes elsewhere. The naive source-only shifts $-r$ and $2-r$ are not both compatible with these two degrees. Sources: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Example 0.6 (cells of $\mathbb CP^n$), SS2.2 (the no-adjacent-cells computation) and SS3.2 (cohomology of $\mathbb CP^n$), and the local packet contract for the corner computation.

items.title: A point and projective-line check of source-first convolution and opposite composition
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited constructible and cellular suppliers. In the point/projective-line geometry of [[ex-unequal-dimensional-proper-pushforwards-have-the-summed-dimension-ext-bm-shift]], let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}(L_1,L_2)$ be the unit $k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ and let $\beta\in\operatorname{Ext}^{1}(L_2,L_1)$ be point evaluation $R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]\to k[1]$, that is, evaluation $H^0(\mathbb P^1,k)\to k$ shifted by $1$ and extended by zero on $H^2$. Then $\alpha*\beta=\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$ in the source-first convention of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], and under the correspondence isomorphism of [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] one has $[\mathbb P^1]*[\mathrm{pt}]=[\mathrm{pt}]$: the refined diagonal intersection of the fundamental class of $\mathbb P^1$ with the point class is the point class, and proper pushforward to the point corner gives its generator.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Route: keep the point/projective-line geometry and the identification $R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)\simeq k\oplus k[-2]$ of [[ex-unequal-dimensional-proper-pushforwards-have-the-summed-dimension-ext-bm-shift]] (Schubert cells and the cellular cochain theorem applied to $\mathbb P^1=\operatorname{Gr}_1(\mathbb C^2)$). Step 1 (the two classes): the unit $\alpha:k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ includes $H^0$ and is the generator of $\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}(L_1,L_2)$; the evaluation map onto $H^0$ followed by the shift gives $\beta:R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]\to k[1]$, the generator of $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}(L_2,L_1)$. Step 2 (composition): $\beta[-1]\circ\alpha:k\to k$ is evaluation of the constant class $1\in H^0(\mathbb P^1,k)$ at the chosen point, hence the identity; by [[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]] this composite is $\Phi^{-1}$ of the convolution product, so $\alpha*\beta=\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$ and $i=j=k=1$ recovers the diagonal unit in the opposite-composition convention. Step 3 (geometric product): $\Phi(\alpha)$ is the positive fundamental class $[\mathbb P^1]\in H^{\mathrm{BM}}_2(\mathbb P^1;k)$ and $\Phi(\beta)$ is the normalized point class $[\mathrm{pt}]\in H^{\mathrm{BM}}_0(\mathbb P^1;k)$, both fixed by the positive complex orientation; the product theorem gives $[\mathbb P^1]*[\mathrm{pt}]=\Phi(\alpha*\beta)=[\mathrm{pt}]$. Concretely, the middle factor is $X_2=\mathbb P^1$, its normal contributes the drop $2d_2=2$, the external-product refined diagonal intersection of the two classes is the point class, and the proper-forgetting pushforward to $Z_{11}=\mathrm{pt}$ integrates it to the generator. This independently checks the middle drop $2$, the source-first order and the absence of an extra shift sign; the swapped corner is not confused with the identity. Sources: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Example 0.6 and SS3.2 (cells and cohomology of $\mathbb CP^n$), and the local packet contract for the convolution check.
